entities.summary:
Wilfrid II, the last bishop of York, played a pivotal role in the history of Anglo-Saxon England. As the see was converted to an archbishopric during his successor's tenure, Wilfrid II's leadership and vision shaped the future of the region. His legacy can be seen in the establishment of the Church of England and the preservation of Anglo-Saxon literature.

Born in the 7th century, Wilfrid II rose to prominence as a missionary and diplomat, traveling extensively throughout Europe and the British Isles. His interactions with the Anglo-Saxon kingdoms had a lasting impact on the region's politics and culture.

In 800 CE, Wilfrid II died, leaving behind a legacy of religious and cultural significance. His successor, Eardwulf, continued his work, solidifying the archbishopric's influence in the region.

Wilfrid II's significance extends beyond his time, as his leadership and vision continue to shape the Church of England and Anglo-Saxon literature. His legacy serves as a reminder of the enduring impact of religious and cultural leaders on the course of history.

The conversion of the see to an archbishopric during Wilfrid II's tenure had significant consequences for the region, leading to the establishment of the Church of England and the preservation of Anglo-Saxon literature.
